commits.pr_title: [Build] Define _USE_MATH_DEFINES for FlashMLA targets
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #53935.

FlashMLA uses `M_LOG2E` in the vLLM extension (`csrc/extension/sm90/dense_fp8/{softmax.h,pybind.cpp}`) and in four upstream files that vLLM compiles into `_flashmla_C` (`api/dense_decode.h`, `smxx/decode/combine/combine.cu`, `sm90/decode/{dense,sparse_fp8}/splitkv_mla.cuh`). MSVC only defines `M_*` when `_USE_MATH_DEFINES` is set before `<cmath>` is included, so both targets fail to build with NVCC+MSVC.

This adds `_USE_MATH_DEFINES` to both targets' compile definitions, guarded by `if(MSVC)` so compile flags on other platforms are untouched. One change covers all six files, and it matches what FlashMLA's own `setup.py` already passes to nvcc. Replacing `M_LOG2E` with a literal in the two extension files (the other option in the issue) would leave `_flashmla_C` broken.


## Test Plan

Minimal MSVC translation unit mirroring `softmax.h` (`#include <cmath>` then `float(M_LOG2E)`), built with and without the define. Linux behaviour is unchanged; existing CI covers `tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla.py`.

## Test Result

```
> cl /nologo /c /EHsc m_log2e_check.cpp
m_log2e_check.cpp(3): error C2065: 'M_LOG2E': undeclared identifier

> cl /nologo /c /EHsc /D_USE_MATH_DEFINES m_log2e_check.cpp
(exit 0)
```

commits.pr_title: [CI] Sample GPU utilization and memory alongside test timelines
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Collect GPU utilization and used/total memory alongside CI command and pytest timing, so the Builds timeline can distinguish GPU-active tests from sampled idle intervals. Dashboard companion: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-dashboard/pull/161.

The existing traced-command wrapper starts one dependency-free sampler per command when `nvidia-smi` is available. It polls up to 16 container-visible NVIDIA devices at a nominal one-second interval and emits 30-second batches of `ci.gpu.sample` events, parented to the command span and authenticated through the existing job-scoped OIDC path. The final batch uses the ordinary job-end spool. No GPU context, pytest-worker sampler, fleet agent, or long-lived dashboard token is introduced.

Queries and periodic uploads have two-second timeouts; repeated device-query failures stop sampling. Shutdown is bounded and preserves the test command's exit status. Periodic upload failures drop a bounded batch rather than retaining unlimited data. Trace export batches now also have a byte budget. Set `CI_INFRA_GPU_SAMPLING=0` to disable collection.

The initial scope is NVIDIA commands in the existing trusted CI tracing rollout. CPU jobs and AMD mirrors remain outside this collection. MIG parent metrics are omitted. Readings represent shared device activity during each test interval, not process-level attribution; short tests and failed uploads can leave gaps.

Checked open PRs for GPU timeline, GPU telemetry, GPU utilization, and ci-otel work; found no existing PR implementing this command-scoped collector. AI assistance was used at the maintainer's request. No model output, accuracy, or serving code changes; model evaluations are not applicable.

## Test Plan

```bash
PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" .venv/bin/python -m pytest .buildkite/scripts/ci-otel/tests/test_ci_otel.py -q
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files .buildkite/scripts/ci-otel/README.md .buildkite/scripts/ci-otel/ci_gpu.py .buildkite/scripts/ci-otel/ci_otel.py .buildkite/scripts/ci-otel/ci_otel.sh .buildkite/scripts/ci-otel/tests/test_ci_otel.py
```

## Test Result

- 40 helper tests passed, including fake-device shell integration, command failure preservation, stop/disable behavior, missing/MIG readings, repeated timeouts, event spool round trip, and count/byte-bounded export.
- All applicable pre-commit checks passed, including Ruff, ShellCheck, mypy, forbidden-import checks, and documentation lint.
- Encoded GPU events were decoded through the dashboard OTLP parser; job-identity authorization, units, and unknown metrics passed. The dashboard companion API returned all real canary samples without truncation; browser verification covered job/command/individual-test charts, zoom, and the explicit missing-sample state for a 475 ms test.

- [Exact PR-head canary #88448](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/88448) passed on commit `01557d74b2185346cd227f584b5bc915287fc42b`: image build plus all six distributed RPC/compile pytest cases passed on two NVIDIA L4s. Production ingestion received 274 samples with a median interval of 1.000 s (p95 1.022 s). Live batches arrived before command completion, final batches arrived at shutdown, and every sample batch matched its command trace/job identity. Peak device memory was 20.7 GiB; low sampled compute utilization remained distinct from allocated memory.
- [Controlled L4 canary #88456](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/88456) passed using the same image and byte-identical collector files on a separate temporary harness branch. All four pytest cases passed: idle readings were 0%, all 40 busy-case readings were 100%, idle retained memory stayed at 0.848 GiB, and release reduced it to 0.254 GiB. Sampling-disabled commands produced no samples; an intentional exit 7 remained exit 7. All 121 samples were ingested with no upload errors.
- Three sampling-on and three sampling-off CUDA benchmark repetitions showed overlapping timing ranges: on 12.697–13.152 s, off 12.491–13.332 s (medians 12.857 / 13.270 s). This small canary found no consistent slowdown; it does not establish a precise overhead bound or validate other GPU types.

Hardware validation covers NVIDIA L4. The dashboard UI was verified locally against the real production-ingested canary data; the companion PR has not been deployed. Deploy the dashboard companion and its seven-day sample retention before enabling collection broadly.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Examples] Launch prefill and decode concurrently in NixlPushConnector demo
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The previous implementation in NixlPushConnector demo fully consumed the prefill response before starting the decode request:

```python
async for _ in self.forward_request(prefill_url, prefill_request, headers):
    continue

generator = self.forward_request(decode_url, decode_request, headers)
return StreamingResponse(generator, media_type="application/json")
```

Since the `async for` loop must finish before execution reaches the decode request, the two upstream requests run sequentially.

This change drains prefill in a background asyncio task and starts the decode stream immediately, allowing both requests to run concurrently.

## Test Plan

Tested with one prefill and one decode vLLM instances on 2 × A100 SXM4 GPUs.
Compared the request timing before and after the patch using the reproduction script below.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction script</summary>

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

VLLM_SRC="${VLLM_SRC:-/workspace/vllm}"
EXP_DIR="${EXP_DIR:-/workspace/nixl-exp}"
MODEL="${MODEL:-Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B}"
VLLM_BIN="${VLLM_BIN:-$VLLM_SRC/.venv/bin/vllm}"
PYTHON_BIN="${PYTHON_BIN:-$VLLM_SRC/.venv/bin/python}"
PROXY_REL="examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_serving/disagg_proxy_pushconnector_demo.py"

mkdir -p "$EXP_DIR"
git -C "$VLLM_SRC" show "HEAD^:$PROXY_REL" > "$EXP_DIR/proxy.before.py"
git -C "$VLLM_SRC" show "HEAD:$PROXY_REL" > "$EXP_DIR/proxy.after.py"

tee "$EXP_DIR/trace_proxy.py" >/dev/null <<'PY'
import importlib.util
import sys
import time

proxy_file = sys.argv.pop(1)
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("push_proxy", proxy_file)
module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(module)

forward_request = module.PushProxy.forward_request
origins = {}


async def traced_forward_request(self, url, data, headers, use_chunked=True):
    role = "prefill" if ":8100" in url else "decode"
    request_id = headers["X-Request-Id"]
    now = time.perf_counter_ns()
    origin = origins.setdefault(request_id, now)

    def trace(event):
        elapsed_ms = (time.perf_counter_ns() - origin) / 1_000_000
        print(f"TIMELINE {request_id} {event} +{elapsed_ms:.3f} ms", flush=True)

    trace(f"{role}_start")
    try:
        async for chunk in forward_request(self, url, data, headers, use_chunked):
            yield chunk
    finally:
        if role == "prefill":
            trace("prefill_end")


module.PushProxy.forward_request = traced_forward_request
args = module.parse_args()
module.PushProxyServer(args=args).run_server()
PY

prefill_pid=""
decode_pid=""
proxy_pid=""

cleanup() {
  for pid in "$proxy_pid" "$decode_pid" "$prefill_pid"; do
    if [[ -n "$pid" ]] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
      kill "$pid"
      wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
  done
  prefill_pid=""
  decode_pid=""
  proxy_pid=""
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

wait_ready() {
  local url="$1"
  for _ in $(seq 1 180); do
    curl -fsS "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 && return 0
    sleep 1
  done
  return 1
}

run_case() {
  local name="$1"
  local proxy_file="$2"
  local case_dir="$EXP_DIR/$name"

  mkdir -p "$case_dir"

  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 \
  UCX_NET_DEVICES=all \
  VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG \
  VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5600 \
    "$VLLM_BIN" serve "$MODEL" \
      --port 8100 \
      --enforce-eager \
      --kv-transfer-config \
      '{"kv_connector":"NixlPushConnector","kv_role":"kv_producer","engine_id":"prefill-engine-001"}' \
      > "$case_dir/prefill.log" 2>&1 &
  prefill_pid=$!

  CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 \
  UCX_NET_DEVICES=all \
  VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG \
  VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_PORT=5601 \
    "$VLLM_BIN" serve "$MODEL" \
      --port 8200 \
      --enforce-eager \
      --kv-transfer-config \
      '{"kv_connector":"NixlPushConnector","kv_role":"kv_consumer","engine_id":"decode-engine-001"}' \
      > "$case_dir/decode.log" 2>&1 &
  decode_pid=$!

  wait_ready http://127.0.0.1:8100/health
  wait_ready http://127.0.0.1:8200/health

  "$PYTHON_BIN" "$EXP_DIR/trace_proxy.py" "$proxy_file" \
    --model "$MODEL" \
    --prefill localhost:8100 \
    --decode localhost:8200 \
    --prefill-engine-id prefill-engine-001 \
    --prefill-kv-host 127.0.0.1 \
    --prefill-side-channel-port 5600 \
    --prefill-tp-size 1 \
    --prefill-pp-size 1 \
    --port 8000 \
    > "$case_dir/proxy.log" 2>&1 &
  proxy_pid=$!

  wait_ready http://127.0.0.1:8000/status

  if ! timeout 120 "$VLLM_BIN" bench serve \
    --backend openai \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --port 8000 \
    --endpoint /v1/completions \
    --model "$MODEL" \
    --dataset-name random \
    --num-prompts 1 \
    --random-input-len 4096 \
    --random-output-len 32 \
    --max-concurrency 1 \
    > "$case_dir/bench.log" 2>&1; then
    cleanup
    echo "benchmark failed" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  cleanup

  grep '^TIMELINE ' "$case_dir/proxy.log" | cut -d ' ' -f 3- \
    > "$case_dir/timeline.txt"
}

run_case before "$EXP_DIR/proxy.before.py"
run_case after "$EXP_DIR/proxy.after.py"

echo "Results: $EXP_DIR"
echo "Before:"
cat "$EXP_DIR/before/timeline.txt"
echo "After:"
cat "$EXP_DIR/after/timeline.txt"
```
</details>

## Test Result

```text
prefill_end +128.740 ms

After:

decode_start +0.863 ms

```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Avoid fastsafetensors deadlock for PP draft models
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

- keep `fastsafetensors` enabled for the target model, where every pipeline stage participates in its WORLD-group collectives;
- fall back to the standard safetensors loader only for an external draft model when PP > 1;
- apply the PP-safe draft load configuration to EAGLE/EAGLE3, DFlash, and DSpark without changing PP=1 or other load formats.

Fixes #50959.

## Why a draft-only fallback

With speculative decoding under pipeline parallelism, the external draft model is instantiated only on the last PP stage. `fastsafetensors` currently uses WORLD-group broadcasts, so ranks on that stage wait for ranks that never enter the draft loader.

Using the stage's TP subgroup is not yet a safe workaround: the installed `fastsafetensors` PyTorch adapter passes subgroup-local source ranks to `torch.distributed` as global ranks. On the second PP stage this fails immediately with `ValueError: Global rank 0 is not part of group`.

The draft checkpoint is much smaller than the target checkpoint, so this PR preserves the fast target load while selecting the existing, collective-free loader for only the draft. The `LoadConfig` is copied, leaving the target configuration unchanged.

## Test plan

### Duplicate-work check

I checked open PRs before implementation. #50514 implements EAGLE3-style speculative decoding with PP, and #53901 extends that work on ROCm; neither fixes the `fastsafetensors` partial-WORLD load tracked by #50959. I did not find another open PR for #50959.

### Unit tests

```bash
uv venv --system-site-packages /tmp/testenv
uv pip install --python /tmp/testenv/bin/python pytest
/tmp/testenv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/worker/test_spec_decode_draft_load_config.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_eagle3_aux_hidden_states_pp.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_spec_decode_embed_sharing_pp.py
```

Result: **39 passed**. Ruff, formatting, mypy, SPDX, and repository pre-commit checks also passed.

### Kimi-K3 DSpark end-to-end

Validated on current `main` (`2c7d7dd64a`) plus the latest #50514 head (`b3b01d5b37`) using 2 nodes × 8 B200 GPUs:

```bash
vllm serve /models/Kimi-K3 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --nnodes 2 \
  --distributed-executor-backend mp \
  --load-format fastsafetensors \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","model":"/models/Kimi-K3-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":5}'
```

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Target load | `fastsafetensors`, 221.77 s |
| Draft load | automatic standard-safetensors fallback, 6.13 s |
| Startup | DSpark CUDA graph capture completed; `/health` returned 200 |
| Generation | one semantic sanity request succeeded; 8/8 concurrent requests returned HTTP 200 |
| Spec decode | 1,055 proposed draft tokens, 623 accepted (59.1%) across 211 draft steps |
| Runtime errors | no `ERROR`, traceback, engine restart, or CUDA fault on either node |

I did not rerun a full model-quality evaluation because this change only selects the loader for draft initialization and does not alter loaded tensors or inference. The generated-output sanity check and nonzero speculative acceptance verify that the draft weights are usable.

AI assistance was used for diagnosis, code editing, testing, and drafting this description. I reviewed the changes and the reported results.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Support `generation` blocks in HF chat template
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Allow the Rust HF renderer to compile chat templates containing `{% generation %}...{% endgeneration %}`. These blocks mark assistant output for Transformers' assistant-token masks and [TRL's assistant-only training loss](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/sft_trainer#train-on-assistant-messages-only). Public examples include the [SmolLM3-3B checkpoint template](https://huggingface.co/HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM3-3B/blob/a07cc9a04f16550a088caea529712d1d335b0ac1/chat_template.jinja#L75-L81) and [TRL's Qwen3 training template](https://github.com/huggingface/trl/blob/42e1cdbafa06d9f7a1c2a7d6cdd98329a55b569f/trl/chat_templates/qwen3_training.jinja#L51-L73). MiniJinja currently rejects the tag with `unknown statement generation`.

Before content-format detection and compilation, rewrite each generation block to `{% call __hf_generation() %}...{% endcall %}`. The callback renders `caller()`, preserving Transformers' local block scope. MiniJinja lexer spans identify statement keywords, preserving whitespace controls, string literals, comments, and raw blocks. The rewrite also validates original `generation`/`call` pairing. This applies to both configured templates and per-request overrides.

Related compatibility handling in other Rust frontends:

- [Mistral.rs](https://github.com/EricLBuehler/mistral.rs/blob/d5ae0f18f2170f10d30880cb7d21fb0880410e7b/mistralrs-core/src/pipeline/chat_template.rs#L816-L819) removes the tags with a regular expression.
- [TGI](https://github.com/huggingface/text-generation-inference/blob/b4adbf2f6e2e721280bd0ea5f91d70f7d033f5ed/router/src/infer/chat_template.rs#L49-L53) removes them with literal replacements.
- [Dynamo's renderer](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/frontend-crates/blob/92cc8bc5f3960a76cd6b92dd348db48a48c83b1f/renderer/src/template/formatters.rs#L212-L216) also uses literal replacements.

This implementation uses scoped call blocks to preserve rendering semantics, including whitespace trimming and assignments inside the block.

Open-PR searches for `generation minijinja`, `generation blocks`, and `endgeneration` found this compatibility gap unaddressed. Implemented with Codex assistance.

## Test Plan

From `rust/`:

```sh
cargo +1.95.0 nextest run -p vllm-chat -E 'test(renderer::hf)'
cargo +1.95.0 clippy -p vllm-chat --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

From the repository root: `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.95.0 pre-commit run`.

## Test Result

- HF renderer suite: 79 passed. Includes 7 rendering-semantics cases, 8 invalid-template cases, and configured/per-request template coverage.
- Clippy and applicable pre-commit hooks passed.
- Separate public-template rendering probe: 8/8 outputs match Transformers for the pinned SmolLM3-3B and TRL Qwen3 training templates, covering thinking enabled/disabled and generation prompt enabled/disabled. Original templates fail compilation in MiniJinja; rewritten templates render successfully. This probe compares rendered text using the actual rewrite module, with a fixed system override for SmolLM3.
- Validation covers template rendering; GPU model-generation evaluation remains outside these results.

commits.pr_title: [3/N] HiSparse: host-resident sparse-MLA decode hot-buffering
commits.pr_body: ## Summary HiSparse adds a host-resident tier beneath vLLM's normal GPU KV cache for sparse-MLA decode. Unlike the original always-host-resident design in #46326, this implementation keeps as much KV as possible in the normal device cache and spills pages to pinned host memory only when GPU capacity must be reclaimed. Supersedes #46326. ## Design overview ```text resident GPU pages | | spill under pressure v pinned host pool ---- selected top-k misses ----> per-request GPU hot buffer ^ | | v +---------------- prefix reuse ---------------- sparse attention ``` The active indexer cache remains device-resident and produces the logical top-k positions needed by sparse attention. A fused CUDA resolver maps each selected position through three possible locations: 1. a normal resident GPU page; 2. an existing row in the request's GPU hot buffer; 3. the pinned host pool. Resident hits return before the hot-cache lookup. Hot hits update a GPU-side LRU, while misses replace LRU entries by gathering only the selected host rows. Resolution, replacement, and LRU updates remain on the GPU and are compatible with CUDA graph replay. HiSparse does not maintain a private host-side copy of indexer KV. The indexer remains a normal prefix-cacheable GPU cache group. When OffloadingConnector is configured alongside HiSparse, generic KV offloading preserves and restores the indexer while HiSparse continues to own only sparse-MLA residency. If the sparse host prefix extends beyond the available indexer prefix, the scheduler restores only the missing indexer suffix, capped at the sparse host boundary. Without generic offloading, the request falls back to the shorter shared prefix and recomputes the remainder. ## Residency and ownership The normal KV cache manager continues to own GPU block allocation. `HiSparseCoordinator` owns logical host blocks, host-prefix identity, and residency transitions. When GPU pressure requires reclaiming a resident page, the coordinator reserves its host destination and sends a transfer command to the worker. The resident GPU block becomes reusable after every worker has acknowledged that the copy is enqueued in stream order. The host page is not published for prefix reuse until every copy has completed. The main components are: - `HiSparseCoordinator`: scheduler-side host allocation, prefix state, and spill policy. - `HiSparseConnector`: carries residency commands and transfer acknowledgements between scheduler and workers. - `HiSparseConnectorWorker`: manages the pinned host-pool lifecycle and executes copies. - `HiSparseRuntime`: owns each cache's host/hot views, GPU LRU state, and fused attention-time resolution. Host blocks use the same token hashes as their resident counterparts, but their hashes are published only after the contents are durable. Spilling therefore preserves prefix-cache value without allowing an incomplete host write to be reused. ## P/D and NIXL integration NIXL remains the P/D transport; HiSparse determines the decoder-side landing policy. The decoder chooses one policy per request during admission: - If the imported prefix fits in the normal GPU pools, NIXL writes it into resident device pages. - Otherwise, the bulk sparse-MLA KV lands in the registered HiSparse host pool. Device-only regions such as the indexer are still imported to GPU, the request receives its fixed hot-buffer allocation, and pages needed immediately are mirrored into resident GPU pages. The two generic connector prerequisites below are intentionally separate from HiSparse: - #53779 lets connectors select externally transferable cache groups while retaining their scheduler group IDs. - #53780 carries stride, capacity, block size, group mapping, and identity per NIXL region, allowing P/D peers with different layouts and memory placement. #53263 is a separate, optional optimization for same-node P/D. It stages device-to-host NIXL reads through decoder GPU memory to avoid UCX's slow TCP loopback path. It is not required by the intended multi-node P/D design. ## Scope This PR implements the NVIDIA sparse-MLA path and includes the staging required for correct local or mixed prefill on a decode worker. Metrics are split into #53782, and DeepSeek V4's compressed cache geometry is split into #53592. ## Preliminary results Preliminary B300 results: AI assistance was used in the preparation of this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Honor HF revisions, offline mode, and cache directory
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Honor `--revision`, `HF_HUB_OFFLINE`, and `HF_HUB_CACHE` when the Rust frontend resolves Hugging Face model files. A requested revision now reaches both frontend loading and the managed Python engine; offline cache misses produce a local error before any Hub request; cache reads and downloads use the configured Hub cache directory. Commit SHAs resolve directly under `snapshots/<sha>`, including caches populated by Python without `refs/<sha>`.

The scope is deliberately limited to these three settings and the SHA lookup needed for revision support. Separate tokenizer revisions, broader authentication options, and legacy/Transformers environment aliases remain separate work.

The broader `hf-hub` 1.0.0 migration is tracked in [vllm-project/vllm#48575](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48575), with dependency and runtime blockers. This PR supplies the focused fixes on 0.5 while that migration proceeds:

- 1.0.0 already handles `HF_HUB_CACHE` and direct SHA cache lookup; upgrading will let us remove these temporary shims.
- 1.0.0 also adds `HF_TOKEN_PATH`, implicit-token controls, and per-download `local_files_only`. We leave the additional authentication support to that upgrade.
- End-to-end revision propagation and translating `HF_HUB_OFFLINE` into an offline policy remain frontend responsibilities with 1.0.0.

## Test Plan

From `rust/`, with `TMPDIR` set to a writable directory:

```bash
cargo fmt -p vllm-text -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-managed-engine -- --check
cargo nextest run -p vllm-text -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-managed-engine --no-fail-fast -E 'not test(roundtrip)'
cargo clippy -p vllm-text -p vllm-chat -p vllm-server -p vllm-cmd -p vllm-managed-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

## Test Result

Formatting, all selected tests, and strict Clippy passed. Coverage includes CLI/bootstrap revision propagation, branch/tag/SHA cache selection, and offline cache hits and misses.

Five local mock-Hub scenarios passed: branch cache hit, SHA cache hit, offline cache miss, and local directory resolution each produced zero HTTP requests; online download used the requested revision and cache directory while retaining credentials from `HF_HOME/token`. The probe validates file resolution and download behavior; GPU inference and model-quality evaluation remain untested.

Implemented with AI assistance (Codex).

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend][Multimodal] Accept preprocessed multimodal gRPC features

## Purpose

Extend the typed multimodal wire foundation merged in #56174 so the Rust gRPC frontend can accept inline preprocessed multimodal features and lower them to native `MmFeatureSpec` values for EngineCore.

This follow-up adds only the missing gRPC transport and semantic checks: protobuf feature payloads, MessagePack decoding, model modality limits, placeholder bounds and non-overlap, content-bound cache identifiers compatible with Dynamo, producer `mm_hash` preservation, and LoRA-specific encoder-cache isolation. - Reuse typed `MmModality`, `TensorDtype`, and `WireTensor::validate_inline()`.
- Remove duplicate dtype, shape, and byte-width validation.

- Retain bounded MessagePack depth/node complexity, tensor-rank validation, inline-data requirements, model limits, and placeholder validation.
- Derive the encoder identifier directly from the original MessagePack bytes and modality using the same domain-separated algorithm as Dynamo.
- Salt adapter-selected identifiers before encoder-cache handoff matching while preserving the producer hash.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Don't evict a remote engine a transfer is still reading from
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`_evict_stale_engines` documents the invariant it relies on:

> Engines with active transfers or pending handshakes cannot be stale:
> - Active transfers touch `_engine_last_active` in `start_load_kv`.

They touch it once. `pull_worker._read_blocks_for_req` stamps it when a read is issued and never again while that read runs, so a transfer that outlives `engine_ttl` — 3600 s by default, and a peer that has lost its NIC holds one indefinitely — leaves its engine looking idle.

Eviction then calls `release_dlist_handle` and `remove_remote_agent` on the state that transfer is reading through. Nothing consults `_recving_transfers`, and the release happens inside NIXL rather than in Python, so the symptom is a worker process that dies without a traceback:

```
Worker proc VllmWorker-0 died unexpectedly (exit code: None), shutting down executor
```

Observed on a 10-prefill/3-decode disaggregated deployment. All three decode workers died within seconds of each other, six seconds after a new-remote handshake — which is where eviction runs — having spent the previous three hours idle, so a batch of TTL-expired engines had accumulated.

This holds back engines with a transfer still in flight. They become evictable again as soon as it finishes or fails, so the memory bound the TTL exists to enforce is unchanged for any engine that is genuinely idle.

## Test Plan

`test_engine_with_inflight_transfer_is_not_evicted` ages an engine past its TTL while a request is still reading from it, asserts nothing is released, then removes the transfer and asserts the engine evicts normally.

## Test Result

Against the unpatched worker the engine is evicted and both `release_dlist_handle` and `remove_remote_agent` are called with a transfer outstanding; patched, neither is.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DSV4.1][Perf] Use AITER mHC for the delayed pre block
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on AMD still runs its mHC block as the eager Torch reference (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4_1/amd/model.py` imports `mhc_pre_delayed_torch` / `mhc_post_torch` directly). DeepSeek-V4 was moved onto the `MHCPreOp` / `MHCPostOp` dispatch layer and reaches AITER (#41946, #43950, #52737), but V4.1 was never migrated, so on MI355X it pays ~141 kernel launches per sublayer seam to Sinkhorn-normalize a 4x4 matrix.

That cost dominates decode. A per-layer census over a captured decode trace on MI355X (gfx950, TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash):

| launches/layer | share | source |
|---:|---:|---|
| 162 | 48.6% | mHC sinkhorn loop (4x4 comb matrix) |
| 122 | 36.6% | mHC pre/post mix + eager RMSNorm |
| 24 | 7.2% | MoE / FFN (already a fused custom op) |
| 12 | 3.6% | dtype casts/copies (bf16<->fp32) |
| 6 | 1.8% | attention + fused norm/quant |
| 4 | 1.2% | TP collective |
| 3 | 0.9% | other |

85% of the layer's 350 launches are mHC. Attributing GPU time through correlation IDs, the Sinkhorn roll-up is 37.5% of kernel time across 6,966 launches per decode step — ahead of `vllm::moe_forward_shared` at 15.4% — and `aten::sum` on `[6, 4, 4]` inputs alone is 21.5%, from 3,120 calls per step on 96-element tensors. Decode ITL on this machine degrades only 1.9x between concurrency 1 and 32 while per-GPU output throughput rises 13x, so the device is far from saturated and the per-step cost is dominated by something fixed rather than by bandwidth or compute.

## Why V4.1 cannot just reuse `MHCPreOp`

V4.1 collapses each sublayer's input with the **previous** sublayer's pre-mix, and returns the current one for the next seam. AITER's `mhc_pre` neither returns its pre-mix nor accepts an incoming one, so it cannot serve that shape as-is.

The staggering does not change the gates, though. Comparing the delayed and non-delayed formulations on identical inputs:

```
post_mix     max_abs_err = 0.000e+00   <- identical
comb_mix     max_abs_err = 0.000e+00   <- identical
layer_input  max_abs_err = 6.41e+00    <- differs (stale coefficients)
```

So the expensive part — the projection, the RMS, the gates and all 20 Sinkhorn iterations, i.e. 141 of the 142 kernels — is bit-identical between the two. Only the collapse differs.

## Approach

AITER exposes its two pre stages separately, and `mhc_pre_big_fuse` consumes the unreduced split-k projection output. This PR drives those stages directly:

1. `mhc_pre_gemm_sqrsum` — projection against `fn` plus row square-sums (1 kernel).
2. `mhc_pre_big_fuse` — post/comb gates and every Sinkhorn iteration (1 kernel). Its collapse applies the current pre-mix, which the delayed form does not want, so it is discarded.
3. New `mhc_pre_mix_triton` epilogue — recovers this seam's pre-mix from the same GEMM output and square-sums that `mhc_pre_big_fuse` already consumed, rather than repeating the projection (1 kernel).
4. `hc_collapse_triton` — the delayed collapse, with the carried coefficients (1 kernel).

New `MHCPreDelayedOp` dispatches AITER -> TileLang -> reference, mirroring `MHCPreOp`. Two cases decline AITER and fall through to TileLang: the model-entry broadcast seam (it projects a narrower operand, `x`, for which there is no AITER equivalent) and a fused RMSNorm (the composed path folds none). `hidden_size` 5120 is also outside `_AITER_MHC_FUSED_RMSNORM_SIZES`, so the fused-RMSNorm variant would not apply here regardless.

## Result

Measured on gfx950, `hidden_size=5120`, `hc_mult=4`, 20 Sinkhorn iterations, against `mhc_pre_delayed_torch`:

| tokens | launches (torch -> aiter) | worst rel err | collapse |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | 141 -> 4 | 2.4e-07 | bit-exact |
| 6 | 141 -> 4 | 5.4e-07 | bit-exact |
| 24 | 141 -> 4 | 6.6e-07 | bit-exact |
| 96 | 141 -> 4 | 8.9e-07 | bit-exact |
| 1024 | 141 -> 4 | 2.2e-06 | bit-exact |
| 16384 | 141 -> 4 | 1.2e-05 | bit-exact |

**35x fewer launches per seam**, worst relative error 1.2e-5, and the collapse is bit-exact because it is the same FP32 multiply-and-sum in both paths. `num_tokens` spans AITER's split-k choices (80 down to 2), which matters because the pre-mix is recovered from that unreduced output.

The model change also routes the three eager `(pre_mix.unsqueeze(-1) * x.float()).sum(dim=1)` collapses (including the DSpark head) through `hc_collapse_triton`, which is bit-exact for that reduction, and the `mhc_post` call sites through `MHCPostOp`.

## Test Plan

- `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py::test_mhc_pre_delayed_rocm_aiter` — AITER vs the delayed reference over tokens 1/2/7/128/1024, both seam variants (carried and model-entry pre-mix), asserting the collapse bit-exact.
- `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py::test_mhc_pre_delayed_rocm_aiter_declines_unsupported` — the broadcast seam and a fused norm must not silently take the AITER path. Asserted by recording which custom op runs, with a positive control so the two declines cannot pass merely because the AITER path is unavailable. (The earlier version checked this by comparing the fallback's output against a Torch reference, which fails for reasons that have nothing to do with this PR: `mhc_pre_big_fuse_with_norm_tilelang` from #56214 is broken on gfx950 with the pinned tilelang 0.1.10, reducing the RMS sum of squares inside a thread-divergent branch and recovering half of it, so `layer_input` comes out sqrt(2) high. Confirmed pre-existing by running the suite on main + #56214 with this PR reverted: the same 15 `test_deepseek_v41_mhc_pre_delayed[fused_norm=True]` cases fail there, and applying this PR leaves the count unchanged. It does not affect serving, since the AMD decoder applies `attn_norm`/`ffn_norm` separately and never passes `norm_weight` into the pre block.)
- End-to-end on MI355X (8x gfx950, TP4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), gsm8k 5-shot via lm-eval:

  | | strict-match | flexible-extract |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | baseline (eager Torch mHC) | 0.9704 ± 0.0047 | 0.9697 ± 0.0047 |
  | this PR (AITER mHC) | 0.9727 ± 0.0045 | 0.9719 ± 0.0045 |

  Within one standard error on both filters, and well clear of the 0.91 gate. The run also exercises the TileLang fallback: `hc_prenorm_gemm_tilelang` compiles 8 times on this branch and never on the baseline, which is the model-entry broadcast seam declining AITER as intended.

  Re-run on the 2026-09-11 nightly (`0.28.1rc1.dev681+ge7edf17ce` + #56214), which is main as it stands rather than the image the row above came from: **0.9719 ± 0.0045** strict-match, 0.9712 ± 0.0046 flexible-extract, 1319/1319 problems.

- Controlled A/B of the block itself, same process and identical input tensors so only the kernel choice differs, under CUDA graphs (`CUDAGraphMode.FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, which is how decode runs here). Microseconds per call, median of 5 x 200 iterations:

  | tokens | torch (main) | tilelang | aiter (this PR) | vs torch | vs tilelang |
  |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 1 | 259.4 | 22.5 | **16.3** | 15.89x | 1.38x |
  | 6 | 263.7 | 23.1 | **16.6** | 15.92x | 1.39x |
  | 12 | 271.4 | 23.2 | **16.8** | 16.15x | 1.38x |
  | 24 | 282.9 | 23.4 | **16.9** | 16.74x | 1.39x |
  | 48 | 303.0 | 27.0 | **17.2** | 17.63x | 1.57x |
  | 96 | 383.3 | 31.3 | **18.0** | 21.30x | 1.74x |
  | 128 | 391.4 | 30.4 | **18.8** | 20.87x | 1.62x |

  Timed eagerly instead, the AITER path is slower than TileLang (93.4 us vs 28.8 us at 1 token): the Python wrapper in `_aiter_ops.mhc_pre_delayed` costs roughly 75 us of host time per call that a captured graph removes. It remains 7.6x-8.2x faster than the Torch reference main runs today, so eager is not a regression against the baseline this PR replaces, but trimming that host overhead is a worthwhile follow-up for `enforce_eager` users.

- The end-to-end ITL figures in the thread below are from a time-driven agentic trace and are *not* a controlled A/B; the table above is the controlled measurement.

## Notes / follow-ups

- `mhc_pre_big_fuse` still writes a collapse we discard. That redundant `[tokens, hidden_size]` bf16 store is the price of composing rather than having a native delayed kernel; it is negligible at decode shapes and ~1-2% of a prefill step. A native `mhc_pre_delayed` in AITER (have the `mhc_pre` epilogue return `pre_mix` and accept an incoming one — `pre_mix` is already computed inside the kernel as a slice of `mixes`, so no new math) would remove both it and the Triton epilogue, taking the seam to 2 launches. Happy to take that up on the AITER side as a follow-up.
- `aiter/jit/module_fused_ar_mhc.so` could additionally fuse the TP all-reduce into the mHC seam (4 collective launches per layer today). AITER already exposes `fused_allreduce_mhc_post_{only,one_stage,split}` and vLLM calls none of them. Out of scope here; tracked in the RFC below.
- Separately observed while profiling and *not* addressed by this PR: ~1,220 AITER GEMM calls per step fall back with `using torch solution:0` for the indexer shapes (`N:128,K:512` and `N:32,K:5120`), i.e. no tuned config on gfx950.

Part of a broader set of ROCm gaps for this model, collected in #56506.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend][gRPC] Surface engine generation errors
commits.pr_body:
Engine failures currently return a successful gRPC response with an `ABORTED` finish reason. Return `INTERNAL` instead for both `Generate` and `GenerateStream`. Streaming keeps output already delivered, then terminates with the error. Genuine client cancellation is unchanged. No protobuf changes.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Kernel][DSV4] Remove tl.constexpr to avoid cold-compile churn in indexer gather kernel
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The generic `_cp_gather_indexer_quant_cache_kernel` declared `NUM_TOKENS`, `NUM_BATCHES`, `BLOCK_TABLE_WIDTH`, and `NUM_BLOCKS` as `tl.constexpr`. All four are shape/batch-derived and vary at runtime (total token at each forward pass, sequences per batch, blocks per sequence), so their values entered the Triton compile-cache key and forced a fresh kernel compile for nearly every distinct shape during serving. This problem becomes more critical for individual local-inference situation when caches are usually cold.

### 4 Parameter breakdown:
`NUM_TOKENS` (**most critical problem, always changing**): can't afford recompilation for EVERY seq_len - this means nearly for every new user prompt, vLLM JIT compiles a new kernel. TTFT explodes and several seconds latency observed.
`NUM_BATCHES`: also changes rapidly under server setup.
`BLOCK_TABLE_WIDTH`, `NUM_BLOCKS`: don't change during each serve session, but making it `tl.constexpr` buys nothing as they are only used once in the kernel as boundary checks.

This mirrors the sibling `_cp_gather_indexer_quant_cache_gfx950_kernel`, which already uses `do_not_specialize=["num_batches"]`. The structural constexprs (`LAYOUT`, `HEAD_DIM`, `BLOCK_TILE_SIZE`, `HEAD_TILE_SIZE`) are unchanged. Pure cache-key change; kernel math and output are unaffected.

commits.pr_title: [BugFix] Fix DP token padding in dflash attention metadata
commits.pr_body:
## Summary
This PR follows up on the fix in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55458, but for dflash-derived speculators. While serving DFlash/DSpark models with DP > 1, the extra padding tokens from the DP sync can cause a mismatch between the number of query tokens reported in `query_start_loc_cpu` and the number reported by `num_tokens` in the attention metadata. When this happens, it can trigger the following assertion for the FlashInfer backend:
```
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py", line 2020, in sample_tokens
  draft_tokens = self.speculator.propose(
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py", line 491, in propose
  self._generate_draft(
File "vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/dflash/speculator.py", line 255, in _run_model
  last_hidden_states = self.model(
File "vllm/model_executor/models/qwen3_dflash.py", line 348, in forward
  hidden_states = self.self_attn(
File "vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py", line 2213, in forward
  prefill_wrapper.run(
File "flashinfer/prefill.py", line 2825, in run
  raise ValueError
ValueError: q.shape[0] (52) does not match qo_indptr[-1] (48). For paged prefill,
q must have shape [total_tokens, num_heads, head_dim] where total_tokens = qo_indptr[-1].
```

I refactored the way we build the attention metadata for the speculators so that this mismatch no longer happens in practice. I created a helper (`_build_uniform_attn_metadata`) which is called by the DFlash and DSpark speculators during proposal of their N draft tokens, and during the last N-1 single draft decodes for MTP and EAGLE. `_build_uniform_attn_metadata` ensures that the attention metadata is built with the padded tokens count (from the batch descriptor) during FULL cudagraph, and the actual number of query tokens otherwise.

After this fix, the above error is no longer triggered by DFlash/DSpark during startup.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Only enforce disk block alignment for O_DIRECT
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`DiskBackend.init` asserts `total_block_bytes % 4096 == 0` unconditionally. That invariant exists only for direct I/O: with `O_DIRECT`, kernel DMA requires block-aligned buffers, file offsets, and transfer lengths. With `use_page_cache=True` the file is opened without `O_DIRECT`, and buffered `preadv`/`pwritev` impose no alignment constraint — but the assert fires before the open flags are decided, rejecting boot entirely.

That makes disk offload unbootable for KV layouts whose per-block stride isn't 4096-aligned, e.g. hybrid models whose per-rank cache tensors sum to a 512-aligned-but-not-4096-aligned size:

```
AssertionError: total_block_bytes=3098112 not aligned to 4096
```

Gate the assert behind `not use_page_cache`; the O_DIRECT path keeps full enforcement.

## Test Plan

```
pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_worker.py -k alignment_only_required_for_direct_io
```

New parametrized test: aligned geometry with page cache (ok), 512-aligned geometry with page cache (ok, and the backing file is created at `num_slots * stride`), same geometry without page cache (`AssertionError` — invariant preserved).

## Test Result

Covered by the new CUDA-gated test in CI.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Fix KDA projection overlap on Hopper
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #55350.

Kimi-K3's low-token-count TP8 KDA projection-overlap path fails during CUDA
graph profiling on H100/SM90a. Two independent incompatibilities are involved:

1. the skinny N/K kernels unconditionally emit PTX `fma.f32.bf16`, which
   requires SM100 or newer and fails libNVVM compilation for `sm_90a`; and
2. FlashInfer's `cute-dsl` QKVG backend rejects SM90 during backend validation.

PR #55108 avoids the failure by disabling KDA projection overlap on Hopper.
This PR keeps the overlap structure enabled while selecting architecture-safe
operations.

## Implementation

- **SM100 and newer:** retain the existing mixed-precision BF16 FMA path.
- **SM90:** convert BF16 operands to FP32 and use FP32 FMA in the skinny N/K
  kernels.
- **SM100 and SM103 QKVG:** retain FlashInfer `cute-dsl` with PDL.
- **Other capabilities, including SM90:** use `torch.mm` for QKVG while keeping
  the concurrent F_A/beta and F_B projection branch.

The architecture check follows the PTX ISA requirement that
`fma.f32.{f16/bf16}` requires `sm_100` or higher. SM100 and SM103 behavior is
otherwise unchanged.

## Test plan and results

### Focused source checks

- `ruff format --check`: passed
- `ruff check`: passed
- Python compilation: passed
- capability and QKVG backend-selection tests: passed locally

### H100 single-GPU compile and correctness preflight

Tested with `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0`, so the projection-overlap path executed:

- skinny N and K kernels compiled for rows 2 through 14;
- CUDA-graph capture and replay passed for rows 2, 8, and 14;
- complete overlapped projection passed for rows 3 and 14;
- complete overlap also passed under CUDA-graph replay for row 14;
- the selected H100 QKVG backend was `torch.mm`; and
- projection overlap remained enabled.

Numerical comparison against FP32 references:

- portable skinny N/K kernels: maximum absolute error
  `1.220703125e-4`;
- complete-overlap QKVG `torch.mm` branch: maximum absolute error
  `4.8828125e-4`; and
- minimum observed cosine similarity: greater than `0.9999998`.

The larger QKVG value is from the `torch.mm` branch, not the portable skinny
FMA implementation.

### Four-node H100 end-to-end check

An integration image based on main commit `e962733e` plus this PR and #53948
was tested on 32 x H100 with TP8/PP4, CUDA graphs, BF16 activations, MXFP4
weights, and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=0`:

- the server completed CUDA-graph profiling and started successfully;
- 4,000/4,000 OpenAI-compatible requests succeeded;
- all responses returned HTTP 200 with the expected prompt and completion-token
  counts; and
- output throughput was 3,437.1 tokens/s across the deployment.

This end-to-end result is a startup, correctness, and regression check rather
than an isolated performance comparison because the image also contained the
unrelated PP prototype from #53948. A matched comparison against #55108's
full-disable approach remains useful follow-up work for quantifying the benefit
of preserving overlap on Hopper.

Generic sparse MLA infrastructure reads model-specific settings from the top-level Hugging Face config. Composite and multimodal models keep those settings in their nested text config, which can make backend initialization, workspace sizing, or JIT warmup fail even though the model is configured correctly.

commits.pr_title: [Spec][V2] Support MTP speculative decoding under pipeline parallelism
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

MTP speculative decoding does not work under pipeline parallelism on the V2 model runner. #50514
landed the generic PP spec-decode transport; this PR covers the MTP-specific gaps that remain on
the PP>1 path.

**Depends on #55745** — a one-line `record_stream` guard in #50514's `broadcast_drafts`, without
which this path trips a device-side `IndexKernel` assert under async launches. It is the bottom
commit here and can be dropped once #55745 merges.

**1. MTP drafters do not implement `SupportsPP`.** The engine refuses to build the draft at all:
```
NotImplementedError: Pipeline parallelism is not supported for this model.
Supported models implement the `SupportsPP` interface.   [DeepSeekMTPModel]
```
The draft runs only on the last PP stage, so it never consumes PP intermediate tensors, but the
interface still requires the `make_empty_intermediate_tensors` factory. Applied to `DeepSeekMTP`
and `Qwen3_5MTP`. Mirrors #39704 for the V1 runner.

**2. Qwen3.5/3.6 MTP draft head skips its `fc` projection.** It branched on `is_first_rank`, which
is False on the last PP stage where the drafter is built. The head then fell through to the
intermediate-tensor path with nothing to read (~1% acceptance). Now branches on
`intermediate_tensors is None`, which is equivalent for a pipelined module and correct for a
whole-drafter-on-one-rank module. @hackxixi suggested this as the general rule for draft heads.

**3. DeepSeek MTP does not load its own `embed_tokens`.** A checkpoint storing it as one top-level
tied weight has no spec layer to rewrite from. The loader dropped it, and the draft embedded with
uninitialised weights. Under PP the target's copy is a `PPMissingLayer` on the draft's stage, so it
cannot borrow the target's. Per-spec-layer checkpoints are unaffected.

**4. `DeepseekV32MTP` carries neither of the above.** It was forked out of `DeepSeekMTP` after this
branch first added `SupportsPP`, and took neither that nor the `embed_tokens` load.
`speculative.py` routes `deepseek_v32` and `glm_moe_dsa` there, so this is the GLM-5.2 and
DeepSeek-V3.2 path. Missing `SupportsPP` raises the error above; the missing `embed_tokens` load is
silent — the engine serves correct output, because rejected drafts are discarded, and only
acceptance shows it: 32.69% against 93.51% once the weight loads. Both restored on the nvidia and
amd variants.

**5. Stale `topk_indices_buffer` in sparse MLA backends.** `LLMBaseProposer.load_model` repoints
the draft's indexers at the target's buffer, but that runs after the backend impls snapshot it in
`__init__`. Its `named_modules()` walk reaches the indexer but not the impls, which are plain
`AttentionImplBase` objects. The impls then read a buffer nothing writes: garbage DSA attention and
degenerate drafts.

A `SharedTopkIndicesBuffer` mixin now resolves the buffer per read, so `forward_mqa` is unchanged
and every `SparseMLACommonImpl` subclass is covered, including `flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90`. The
three impls that are not subclasses (`flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm120`, `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse`,
`xpu_mla_sparse`) use the same mixin. An explicit assignment still supersedes the indexer, which is
how skip-topk layers and the proposer's module walk set it. The mixin is in
`sparse_mla_attention.py`, not `v1/attention/backend.py`: every consumer is sparse MLA, and the
four span two bases whose only shared ancestor is `AttentionImplBase`.

`DeepseekV32Model` (nvidia) held the buffer in a local, so the proposer's sharing block never ran
for DSA at all. It is now exposed on the model, as the ROCm variant already does.

**6. Draft MM embedding gather on ranks without an encoder runner.** `ModelState.encoder_runner`
exists only on the first PP rank, so a multimodal-capable MTP drafter died in warmup on the last:
```
AttributeError: 'MambaHybridModelState' object has no attribute 'encoder_runner'
```
Later ranks have no cached embeddings to gather. `Qwen3_5MTP` is the first in-tree draft that is
both `SupportsPP` and `SupportsMultiModal`.

## Not duplicating existing work

- #50514 provides the PP draft-token transport. The earlier revision of this PR carried its own
  version; that is dropped. The only change here to `v1/worker/gpu/pp_utils.py` is #55745's guard.
- #53408, #54635, #55081 (@JasonKeyiL) implement `SupportsPP` on other MTP families; neither
  `deepseek_mtp.py` nor `qwen3_5_mtp.py` is touched by any of them. #55081 overlaps fix 4's
  `SupportsPP` half, which can be dropped if it merges first.
- #54709 (qwen4_exp draft head) is the same bug as fix 2 and takes the same one-liner; left out to
  keep this focused.

## Test Plan

```
VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.2-FP8 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --pipeline-parallel-size 2 \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":1}'
```

New unit tests in `tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py` cover fix 5: the repointed-buffer
regression itself, explicit assignment superseding the indexer, and the subclass family.

## Test Result

```
# 1x H200 NVL (SM 9.0)
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_sparse_mla_sm120_api.py \
  tests/kernels/attention/test_flashmla_sparse.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_glm5next_sparse.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_mask.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py    -> 186 passed, 616 skipped
pytest tests/v1/worker/test_pp_utils.py                        -> 4 passed
pytest tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/test_mtp_parallel_load.py      -> 5 passed, 1 skipped
pytest tests/models/test_qwen3_5_mtp_config.py \
```

Skips are capability and dtype gates (SM 10.x, `fp8_ds_mla`/`nvfp4_ds_mla`, FA4, `block_size=32`),

### Acceptance

`tests/v1/e2e/spec_decode/acceptance_rates/`.

## Purpose

Currently, this page indicates that /inference is both protected by the api-key and also vulnerable by default. 
Indeed, it currently displays

commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

This PR reverts #53664 ("[Rocm][Kimi-k3] Fix pipeline_parallel support for the kimik3 DCP mode"). That PR added a fallback in `MLAAttentionLayer.build()` that derives `dcp_local_seq_lens` from `seq_lens` whenever `CommonAttentionMetadata` does not carry it, together with an assert and two test-registry entries. The fallback is dead code: in vLLM's in-tree paths, `dcp_local_seq_lens` is always populated before the MLA decode path runs whenever DCP is enabled.

Evidence:

- The monolithic V1 model runner populates `CommonAttentionMetadata.dcp_local_seq_lens` unconditionally when `decode_context_parallel_size > 1` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py:2456-2466`), and this has been in place since before #53664 was authored.
- The modular model runner (MRV2) does the same via `maybe_prepare_dcp_local_seq_lens()` right before attention metadata is built, after PCP batch partitioning (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_runner.py:1728`, helper in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cp_utils.py`). The helper returns `None` only when `dcp_size == 1`, in which case the MLA layer's `dcp_world_size` is also 1 and the branch is never taken, so the fallback is unreachable.
- Both runners always set `seq_lens` on `CommonAttentionMetadata`, so the assert added by #53664 is likewise unreachable.

Keeping the fallback would also mask future regressions in runner-side population: if a path ever stopped populating `dcp_local_seq_lens`, the layer would silently derive it instead of failing loudly. Removing it restores a single source of truth for DCP-local sequence lengths (the model runner). The two test-registry entries added by #53664 are removed along with the revert.
